newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-WH Smith to stage profit comeback.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-WH Smith to stage profit comeback.

text.p: British bookseller and newspaper distribution firm W.H. Smith Group Plc is expected to more than double first half profits when it reports results on Wednesday.
Retail analysts predicted pretax profits in the half year would rise to between 36.0 million and 38.5 million stg, from 17.3 million for the same period a year ago.
The retailer, which reported its first ever loss last year, is looking in better shape after shedding its office supplies business and its half share of loss-hit home improvement chain Do It All.

But analysts said the group still faced a big challenge securing the long-term future of its main High Street chain W.H. Smith. The stores' traditional market has been invaded by food superstores, which now also sell many items shoppers traditionally bought at Smiths - books, videos, greeting cards and stationery.

Analysts agreed that chief executive Bill Cockburn, brought in last January to revive the business, had done a good job so far, but expressed reservations about his chances of revitalising the core chain.
"His initial actions - selling Do It All and business supplies - were positive, but W.H. Smith is more difficult," said one retail analyst.
The stores have massive "footfall" and a well-loved brand name, but the tricky issue for Smith's management is how to convert this into stronger sales, analysts said.
Sales in the core business W.H. Smith Retail are likely to have been volatile, but analysts expected Smiths to have had a reasonable Christmas after a slack autumn.
Waterstones, Smith's specialist bookshop, is expected to have performed well, but Smith's Virgin/Our Price music stores may have lost share in a highly competitive market.

The group has been tipped as a bid target more than once since its problems surfaced in 1995. But analysts dismissed the recent flurry of takeover speculation. "I don't think it had a lot of credibility, the business looks less vulnerable this year than last," said another retail analyst.

The shares, which did well in the early part of last year, have been poor performers since full year results were published in August. Since then, they have underperformed the retail sector by about 10 percent and the market by about 20 percent.
"The share price has come back to earth because phase two of the restructuring is more longer term and difficult to produce," said another retail analyst, who recommended them as a "hold."
Smiths is expected to pay an unchanged dividend of 5.25 pence, or offer a slight increase to 5.5 pence.
